gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-thai: Junegull draws every curve in one steady line, pinched shut at the mouth. Noto Sans Thai swells into inflated glass beads, rounded and left open, so the retro heading gets a friendlier plain sans beneath it.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Cast iron capitals seem to stand behind every lowercase letter in Junegull, its curves matching the stems in width. Noto Sans Thai Looped runs tall and open, so paragraphs of it would read with a bold, spacious steadiness.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tifinag: Friendly and a bit retro, Junegull draws downstrokes and connecting curves with no shift in weight. Noto Sans Tifinagh fills the line with rounded, open bowls, so extended reading feels inviting rather than stiff.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Blunt, retro charm up top: Junegull pinches every curve shut while Noto Sans Tirhuta cuts its terminals back to leave big gaps. Junegull makes the loud entrance; the sans quietly carries the text.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and clean, its letter mouths left open like a chalk arc never joined. And Junegull holds its thickness steady around every curve, so the closed heading feels sealed beside that open text.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-vai: Retro signage energy: Junegull keeps a single track width, closed and pinched, like a neon sign tube. While Junegull is best at punch, Noto Sans Vai is best at words that read as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Noto Sans Vithkuqi reads clean and modern, with open throats. The standout quality is steadiness: Junegull has no calligraphic thinning, and the sans barely steps down from capital to lowercase.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho hits the page with a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed hard, and an e with a wide terminal gap. And the real pull is friction: closed, pinched Junegull set against an open-mouthed body.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Words here read as solid blocks, not skylines, with wide channels leading into each counter. Noto Sans Warang Citi handles steady reading, while Junegull, traced at one stylus width, handles the loud entrance.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-yi: Junegull has no calligraphic thinning and keeps its curves closed. Noto Sans Yi, deep through the midsection with rounds left unlatched like a hook, gives that closed retro look somewhere to breathe.
